title: Inquest nears into fatal Christmastime police shooting of London man
article: A hearing over the scope of an inquest into the police shooting death of a London computer programmer will be held Monday.

The hearing is the first stage of inquest into the death of Samuel Maloney, 35, who died in a barrage of gunfire after shooting an officer with a crossbow and charging at others with a hatchet during a Dec. 23, 2016, police raid on his Old South home.

No date has been set yet for the inquest, which is mandatory when someone in custody dies of something other than natural causes. It will be overseen by Dr. David Eden. Roger Shallow and Elizabeth Brown will be inquest counsel.

Coroner's inquests probe the manner and cause of an individual's death. A jury will give recommendations at the end, but won't assign blame.
The inquest will be the third examination of Maloney's death.
Ontario's police watchdog, the Special Investigations Unit (SIU), and an internal London police review both previously cleared all of the officers involved in the fatal shooting of any wrongdoing.

Investigators obtained a warrant on Dec. 21, 2016, to search Maloney's home weeks after a manifesto that included anti-Semitic material was sent to newsletter subscribers at the Hyland Cinema, the SIU said. Facciolo managed the theatre's website and sent out email bulletins, while Maloney was helping develop its software, the SIU report said

Tactical officers forced their way into the house at 56 Duchess Ave., where police entered a computer room and found Maloney and his common-law wife, Melissa Facciolo. Maloney fired a crossbow at an officer, prompting him to fire three shots at Maloney, striking him once, the watchdog said.

Facciolo ran to a rear bedroom, where two officers were inside with the couple's children, while an officer ordered Maloney out of the room with his hands up. But he came out wielding a hatchet and charged toward the bedroom where the two officers and his family were holed up, the SIU said.

One of the officers fired five shots at Maloney, striking him three times in the chest. Maloney fell to the ground near the bedroom door before a third officer shot him once in the head, the SIU said.
